raw: {"contentVerdict":"DEFECT","defectClass":"Unframed synthetic or unsupported empirical citation presented as fact","severity":"HIGH","shouldBlock":true,"evidenceSpans":["A 2016 Stanford study of 4,200 first-time managers found that those who ran weekly one-on-ones were 2.3 times more likely to retain their reports over two years.","The effect held across every industry the researchers sampled."],"rationale":"The candidate presents a highly specific empirical research claim as real source-backed fact, naming Stanford, a year, sample size, retention multiplier, time window, and industry-wide generalization, but gives no reader-visible framing that this may be an invented example, hypothetical scenario, or illustrative data. For source-register judging, that makes the passage misleading on its face because a reader would naturally understand it as reporting an actual study rather than illustrative or synthetic material."}
